# Architecture Report

`mxcli report architecture` turns the catalog's reference graph into a page a team
can read: each app module on its layer, module health, the coupling matrix in layer
order, bounded contexts (Leiden clusters × modules), god nodes, bridges, entity
hotspots, cycles with the exact edges that close them, and unused documents.

The command does the measuring. This skill is the judgement it cannot make.

## Run it

```bash
# measure once, keep the data
mxcli report architecture -p app.mpr --format json -o docs/architecture/arch.json
# render with a person's names and verdicts, as often as needed
mxcli report architecture --from docs/architecture/arch.json \
  --annotations docs/architecture/notes.yaml -o docs/architecture/architecture.html
```

Marketplace modules, `System` and `MxTest` are outside the app by default — they
dominate god nodes and coupling otherwise. `--include-marketplace` brings them in;
`--modules A,B` or `--exclude C` choose the app's modules by hand.

## Checks before you trust the page

1. **Domain versus navigation.** Layers, the matrix and cycles use domain edges
   only; menus, layouts and page links are listed under "Navigation dependencies".
   The stat "N with navigation counted" shows what the page would claim otherwise —
   on a 14-module app every module was in one cycle until navigation was split out.
   Do not "fix" a navigation cycle: the shell links every screen by design.
2. **"Dead" needs a second look.** Every entry under *Unused documents* marked
   `verify` names why the graph cannot see a use: a microflow named in a constant
   (`OIDC.GlobalUserProvisioningMicroflow`), a snippet in a layout region when the
   catalog has no layout references, a name in text. Search for the name before
   deleting anything. Java actions calling a microflow are invisible too (#1819).
3. **Cluster labels are not names.** A cluster is labelled by its dominant module and,
   when that collides, its most central member. Name each one from its members in
   the annotations file — three clusters all called after one big module is the
   normal case, not an error.

## Reading it

- **Low cohesion is fine for a shell, an admin UI or an adapter.** The page names
  the role when the model shows it (mostly navigation edges; mostly services and
  mappings; an admin-named module). For any other low-cohesion module, ask whether
  it is two modules.
- **Judging a cycle.** Each cycle lists its edges and the lightest one. A cycle is
  *real* when both directions carry domain meaning (orders need invoices, invoices
  read orders); it is *accidental* when one direction is a helper that belongs on
  the other side — usually the lightest edge. Record the verdict as
  `cycle:<A+B>`.
- **When a cluster suggests a split.** A module with a fifth or more of its
  clustered documents in each of two clusters may hold two contexts. Check the
  members: shared reference data is not a second context; two workflows that share
  no entity are.
- **Bridges** (betweenness) are where a split would cut; a bridge that is a
  utility microflow is a candidate for a shared module.

## Annotations file

```yaml
title: Architecture — Shop
summary: Two real cycles, both through Pricing; Shell is the app shell.
items:
  "module:Shell": {note: "app shell: layouts and menu"}
  "cluster:Orders.Order": {name: "Order intake", note: "Orders + half of Pricing"}
  "cycle:Billing+Sales": {status: accidental, note: "move SUB_Total to Billing"}
  "unused:Admin.OldExport": {status: unused, note: "confirmed, remove in 4.2"}
recommendations:
  - Move Sales.SUB_Total into Billing to break the cycle.
```

Keys the page prints but the file has no entry for are simply unannotated; entries
that match nothing are listed at the bottom of the page so stale verdicts are seen.
